run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: Hotel Reservation
Namespace: hotel-reservation

A hotel reservation application built with Go and gRPC, providing backend in-memory and persistent databases, a recommender system for hotel recommendations, and a functionality to place reservations.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: Investigated the hotel-reservation namespace across metrics, traces, logs, Kubernetes state and events, starting from the only alerting signal present: a pending KubePodNotReady for pod hotel-reservation/audit-log-archiver-29920953-c4j9v. The hotel reservation request path shows no observed failure in the sampled window: all 19 deployments report 1/1 ready and available, every application pod and every MongoDB/Memcached/Consul dependency pod is Running with Ready=True and restartCount 0, all eight blackbox probes of the app services return probe_success=1 with 2-3 ms probe duration, sampled frontend HTTP spans carry http.status_code=200 (including POST /reservation), and per-service span p95 latency is at most ~5 ms (frontend 4.97 ms, search 2.44 ms, all other services below 1 ms). One caveat limits error analysis: traces_span_metrics_calls_total exposes only STATUS_CODE_UNSET for every hotel-reservation service, so error rate cannot be derived from span status here. The single entity with its own failure evidence is CronJob hotel-reservation/audit-log-archiver: its archiver container completes and exits (terminated reason Completed) while its fluent-bit-sidecar runs an endless 'exec nc -lk -p 24224 -e cat' with no probes, no ttlSecondsAfterFinished and no activeDeadlineSeconds, so each per-minute Job never finishes, archiver pods accumulate and stay ContainersNotReady, which is exactly the pending KubePodNotReady alert. That workload is not on the hotel reservation request path, so no hotel-app impact is demonstrated. I also found pre-staged privilege-revocation tooling: ConfigMaps failure-admin-geo and failure-admin-rate hold scripts revoking readWrite on geo-db / rate-db from the MongoDB 'admin' user, and the volume is mounted into exactly mongodb-geo and mongodb-rate, both at deployment generation 2 (a second scaled-down ReplicaSet exists for each). However no evidence shows the scripts ran or had any effect: mongod logs contain no authorization-failure lines, the init scripts granted readWrite successfully at 10:32:42 (geo) and 10:32:44 (rate), and no app errors or 5xx were observed. The wrk2 load generator recorded 192 socket timeouts per 30 s round against the frontend ClusterIP while reporting no Non-2xx responses and a 10.26 ms max recorded latency, which remains an unexplained client-side observation rather than a demonstrated server fault.

claims.text: All 19 hotel-reservation deployments report replicas=1 with readyReplicas=1 and availableReplicas=1 (consul, frontend, geo, jaeger, memcached-profile/rate/reserve, mongodb-geo/profile/rate/recommendation/reservation/user, profile, rate, recommendation, reservation, search, user).

Every hotel-reservation application pod and every dependency pod (frontend, geo, profile, rate, recommendation, reservation, search, user, consul, jaeger, memcached-profile/rate/reserve, mongodb-geo/profile/rate/recommendation/reservation/user) is phase Running with Ready=True and restartCount 0; only the audit-log-archiver pods are Ready=False with reason ContainersNotReady ('containers with unready status: [archiver]').

Prometheus reports up=1 for every hotel-reservation scrape target and every blackbox probe of the app services (frontend.hotel-reservation:5000, geo:8083, profile:8081, rate:8084, recommendation:8085, reservation:8087, search:8082, user:8086).

probe_success=1 for all eight hotel-reservation service probes (probe_duration_seconds 2.1-2.8 ms), while the only failing probe in the namespace is blackbox-ingress-hotel-reservation (probe_success=0, probe_http_status_code=0) which targets http://ingress-nginx-controller.ingress-nginx/api/hotels.

Sampled span latencies for the app are low: histogram_quantile(0.95) of traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket is 4.97 ms for frontend, 2.44 ms for search, 0.98 ms rate, 0.96 ms profile, 0.96 ms reservation, 0.95 ms recommendation, 0.95 ms user and 0.95 ms geo; the highest operation-level p95 is frontend HTTP POST /reservation at 20.5 ms.

frontend HTTP server spans in the sampled traces carry http.status_code=200 (HTTP GET /hotels, HTTP GET /recommendations, HTTP POST /user, HTTP POST /reservation all 200) with durations of roughly 0.5-9 ms, and the trace rows are flagged with zero errors by visible tags.

traces_span_metrics_calls_total for namespace hotel-reservation exposes only status_code=STATUS_CODE_UNSET for all eight services (frontend, geo, profile, rate, recommendation, reservation, search, user), so span-status error rate cannot be derived for this application.

The only not-ready pods in the cluster are the audit-log-archiver pods in hotel-reservation (5 Running with Ready=False plus 1 Pending with waiting reason ContainerCreating at query time), accumulating one new pod per minute with restartCount 0.

CronJob hotel-reservation/audit-log-archiver runs every minute (schedule * * * * *, concurrencyPolicy Allow, backoffLimit 0, no ttlSecondsAfterFinished, no activeDeadlineSeconds) and its two busybox:1.36 containers (archiver, fluent-bit-sidecar) define no readinessProbe and no livenessProbe; the sidecar command is 'exec nc -lk -p 24224 -e cat', which never exits.

The archiver container of pod audit-log-archiver-29920953-c4j9v logs 'archiver: starting audit log archive', 'archiver: audit record forwarded' and 'archiver: upload complete (0 bytes archived); record=audit-archive-ready' within ~3 seconds and then exits, and kube_pod_container_status_terminated_reason reports container archiver reason=Completed for that pod while the sidecar keeps the pod alive.

The only alert with any state in the Prometheus alerting rules is KubePodNotReady, pending since 2026-11-21T10:34:09Z for pod audit-log-archiver-29920953-c4j9v in namespace hotel-reservation; HighRequestErrorRate, HighRequestLatency, HighRequestRate, DeploymentNotReady, PodStatusError and MessageConsumerLag are all inactive.

ConfigMap hotel-reservation/failure-admin-geo contains revoke-admin-geo-mongo.sh, which runs db.revokeRolesFromUser('admin',[{role:'readWrite',db:'geo-db'}]) (plus remove-admin-mongo.sh dropping user 'admin', and matching restore scripts), and ConfigMap failure-admin-rate contains the equivalent script for db 'rate-db'.

Deployment mongodb-geo (generation 2) and Deployment mongodb-rate (generation 2) both mount a 'failure-script' volume from ConfigMaps failure-admin-geo / failure-admin-rate alongside their init-script ConfigMaps, whereas mongodb-profile (generation 1) only mounts its data volume; the mongodb-geo pod additionally mounts /scripts from failure-admin-geo in its container.

No authorization or privilege-change evidence appears in the hotel-reservation logs inside the window: a Loki search over the namespace for 'authorization|Unauthorized|not authorized|revokeRoles|dropUser|createUser|grantRoles' returned only the two mongod startup 'Options set by command line ... security.authorization' lines, and mongod startup logged successful readWrite grants and 'Initialization script completed' at 10:32:42 for geo-db and 10:32:44 for rate-db.

The wrk2 load-generator pod wrk2-job-9j999 reported for two consecutive 30 s rounds against http://10.96.186.110:5000 (frontend ClusterIP): '2971 requests in 30.04s / 30.03s, 1.21/1.23MB read', 'Socket errors: connect 0, read 0, write 0, timeout 192', recorded latency max 10.26 ms and mean 3.71 ms, and a search of its log for 'Non-2xx' returned no lines.

Observability history here is very short: Loki holds hotel-reservation lines only from 2026-11-21T10:32:35Z onward (a 5-minute count_over_time returns a single point at 10:33:44 with 1169 lines), Prometheus series carry a single sample at 10:34:21, and the sampled Jaeger traces cover roughly 10:33:56-10:34:20, so no comparable pre-incident baseline exists.

The object that produces the observed not-ready state is CronJob hotel-reservation/audit-log-archiver: its job template pairs a short-lived archiver container with an endless sidecar ('exec nc -lk -p 24224 -e cat') and defines neither probes, ttlSecondsAfterFinished nor activeDeadlineSeconds, so every per-minute Job stays active forever, each pod keeps a Completed archiver container and never becomes Ready, which explains the pending KubePodNotReady alert without any hotel-reservation application fault.

The intended application-level fault is most plausibly the geo-db or rate-db privilege revocation staged through ConfigMaps failure-admin-geo / failure-admin-rate, which are mounted only into mongodb-geo and mongodb-rate (both rolled to generation 2): if revoke-admin-(geo|rate)-mongo.sh were executed, the 'admin' user used by the geo/rate services would lose readWrite and their MongoDB operations would fail. This remains unconfirmed because no such failure was observed in the sampled window.

The 192 per-round socket timeouts recorded by wrk2 could indicate that a fraction of client connections to the frontend ClusterIP receive no response, but no server-side long spans, non-2xx responses or frontend error log lines were observed in the traced window, so the cause (client-side, service/kube-proxy path, or the load generator itself) is not established.

Against an active geo-db/rate-db privilege fault: mongod logs contain no authorization-failure entries, the init scripts granted readWrite to the 'admin' user at 10:32:42 (geo) and 10:32:44 (rate), all app pods are Ready with 0 restarts, all eight service probes succeed, and the sampled frontend spans (including GET /hotels and POST /reservation) are HTTP 200 with single-digit millisecond durations.

Against a resource-exhaustion explanation for the hotel-reservation pods: the container_cpu_cfs_throttled_periods_total rate is 0 for every container in the namespace, and container CPU usage is at most ~0.047 cores (search-567bb6c4b8-qnp7h), ~0.046 (frontend-68745cb99c-cl45r), ~0.030 (rate-65d6967c95-cjvtl).

Rejected as an explanation for app impact: the failing blackbox-ingress-hotel-reservation probe (probe_success=0, probe_http_status_code=0) targets the ingress-nginx controller's URL, not any hotel-reservation service endpoint, while all eight direct service probes in the same namespace return probe_success=1; the probe failure therefore does not evidence a fault in the hotel-reservation application services I measured.

If the not-ready archiver pods are undesired, fix them at the CronJob level: bound the sidecar lifetime or give the containers a readiness/liveness probe, or make the one-shot archiver a Job that terminates (drop the eternal 'nc -lk' sidecar), and set ttlSecondsAfterFinished/activeDeadlineSeconds; no change was made during this read-only investigation.

Because the geo-db and rate-db privilege-revocation scripts are already mounted into the running mongodb-geo and mongodb-rate pods, a human should confirm with the experiment owner whether revoke-admin-geo-mongo.sh or revoke-admin-rate-mongo.sh was executed after 10:32:48 (and when), and re-check mongod for authorization-failure entries and geo/rate error logs at that time.

gaps: No observability history exists before roughly 2026-11-21T10:32:35Z in Loki, ~10:33:56Z in Jaeger and a single Prometheus sample at 10:34:21Z, so no baseline or earlier incident state could be compared and no latency/error trend can be established.

Whether the ingress tier exists in this cluster could not be established: the queries for Ingress objects across all namespaces and for pods in namespace ingress-nginx both returned no items (no_data), which shows only that those queries matched nothing; the failing blackbox-ingress-hotel-reservation probe therefore cannot be attributed or dismissed beyond noting it targets the ingress URL rather than a hotel-reservation service endpoint.

No MongoDB exporter metric exists (only prometheus_sd_consul_* names matched *mongo*/*consul*/*memcach*/*redis*), so mongod-level privilege, op-counter and connection state cannot be measured directly; geo/rate DB behaviour had to be inferred from logs and app telemetry.

Whether revoke-admin-geo-mongo.sh or revoke-admin-rate-mongo.sh (or remove-admin-mongo.sh) was actually executed inside mongodb-geo/mongodb-rate, and when, is unknown: such exec output is not written to container stdout, and no authorization-failure entries were seen in the sampled window.

The 192 per-round socket timeouts from wrk2 could not be attributed: the wrk2 pod's logs are not readable through the Kubernetes API (HTTP 403 SOURCE_FORBIDDEN, only Loki copies available), its round #2 report falls after the last Loki line at 10:33:52Z, and no server-side slow spans or non-2xx responses were captured.

Error status cannot be computed from traces_span_metrics_calls_total because every hotel-reservation series is STATUS_CODE_UNSET; 5xx detection relied only on sampled span http.status_code tags and log searches, which are not exhaustive.
Kubernetes objects were read at query time (10:34Z-10:41Z), after the authorized data snapshot, so pod and deployment state is not proof of state during the incident window.

No change-history integration is available, so any change to the failure-admin-geo / failure-admin-rate ConfigMaps or to the mongodb-geo / mongodb-rate deployment templates before the window could not be dated.
next_steps: Ask the experiment owner to confirm whether the geo-db or rate-db 'admin' readWrite revocation was applied and at what time, then correlate it with mongod authorization-failure log entries.

Verify the MongoDB privileges directly in mongodb-geo (geo-db) and mongodb-rate (rate-db) with db.getUser('admin'), for example via the already-mounted /scripts helpers, to establish the current role set.

If the intent is only to stop the alert noise, rework the audit-log-archiver CronJob so its pod can complete (remove the eternal sidecar or add probes/ttl) instead of leaving accumulating not-ready pods and a standing KubePodNotReady alert.

Capture a longer baseline of the frontend (span metrics and several wrk2 rounds) to determine whether the 192 socket timeouts per 30 s round are steady-state client-side behaviour or a real service-path problem.
Determine whether an ingress tier is expected in this cluster at all, since the blackbox-ingress-hotel-reservation probe currently has nothing to target.

Every hotel-reservation application pod and every dependency pod (frontend, geo, profile, rate, recommendation, reservation, search, user, consul, jaeger, memcached-profile/rate/reserve, mongodb-geo/profile/rate/recommendation/reservation/user) is phase Running with Ready=True and restartCount 0; only the audit-log-archiver pods are Ready=False with reason ContainersNotReady ('containers with unready status: [archiver]').

Prometheus reports up=1 for every hotel-reservation scrape target and every blackbox probe of the app services (frontend.hotel-reservation:5000, geo:8083, profile:8081, rate:8084, recommendation:8085, reservation:8087, search:8082, user:8086).

probe_success=1 for all eight hotel-reservation service probes (probe_duration_seconds 2.1-2.8 ms), while the only failing probe in the namespace is blackbox-ingress-hotel-reservation (probe_success=0, probe_http_status_code=0) which targets http://ingress-nginx-controller.ingress-nginx/api/hotels.

Sampled span latencies for the app are low: histogram_quantile(0.95) of traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket is 4.97 ms for frontend, 2.44 ms for search, 0.98 ms rate, 0.96 ms profile, 0.96 ms reservation, 0.95 ms recommendation, 0.95 ms user and 0.95 ms geo; the highest operation-level p95 is frontend HTTP POST /reservation at 20.5 ms.

frontend HTTP server spans in the sampled traces carry http.status_code=200 (HTTP GET /hotels, HTTP GET /recommendations, HTTP POST /user, HTTP POST /reservation all 200) with durations of roughly 0.5-9 ms, and the trace rows are flagged with zero errors by visible tags.

traces_span_metrics_calls_total for namespace hotel-reservation exposes only status_code=STATUS_CODE_UNSET for all eight services (frontend, geo, profile, rate, recommendation, reservation, search, user), so span-status error rate cannot be derived for this application.

The only not-ready pods in the cluster are the audit-log-archiver pods in hotel-reservation (5 Running with Ready=False plus 1 Pending with waiting reason ContainerCreating at query time), accumulating one new pod per minute with restartCount 0.

CronJob hotel-reservation/audit-log-archiver runs every minute (schedule * * * * *, concurrencyPolicy Allow, backoffLimit 0, no ttlSecondsAfterFinished, no activeDeadlineSeconds) and its two busybox:1.36 containers (archiver, fluent-bit-sidecar) define no readinessProbe and no livenessProbe; the sidecar command is 'exec nc -lk -p 24224 -e cat', which never exits.

The archiver container of pod audit-log-archiver-29920953-c4j9v logs 'archiver: starting audit log archive', 'archiver: audit record forwarded' and 'archiver: upload complete (0 bytes archived); record=audit-archive-ready' within ~3 seconds and then exits, and kube_pod_container_status_terminated_reason reports container archiver reason=Completed for that pod while the sidecar keeps the pod alive.

The only alert with any state in the Prometheus alerting rules is KubePodNotReady, pending since 2026-11-21T10:34:09Z for pod audit-log-archiver-29920953-c4j9v in namespace hotel-reservation; HighRequestErrorRate, HighRequestLatency, HighRequestRate, DeploymentNotReady, PodStatusError and MessageConsumerLag are all inactive.

ConfigMap hotel-reservation/failure-admin-geo contains revoke-admin-geo-mongo.sh, which runs db.revokeRolesFromUser('admin',[{role:'readWrite',db:'geo-db'}]) (plus remove-admin-mongo.sh dropping user 'admin', and matching restore scripts), and ConfigMap failure-admin-rate contains the equivalent script for db 'rate-db'.

Deployment mongodb-geo (generation 2) and Deployment mongodb-rate (generation 2) both mount a 'failure-script' volume from ConfigMaps failure-admin-geo / failure-admin-rate alongside their init-script ConfigMaps, whereas mongodb-profile (generation 1) only mounts its data volume; the mongodb-geo pod additionally mounts /scripts from failure-admin-geo in its container.

No authorization or privilege-change evidence appears in the hotel-reservation logs inside the window: a Loki search over the namespace for 'authorization|Unauthorized|not authorized|revokeRoles|dropUser|createUser|grantRoles' returned only the two mongod startup 'Options set by command line ... security.authorization' lines, and mongod startup logged successful readWrite grants and 'Initialization script completed' at 10:32:42 for geo-db and 10:32:44 for rate-db.

The wrk2 load-generator pod wrk2-job-9j999 reported for two consecutive 30 s rounds against http://10.96.186.110:5000 (frontend ClusterIP): '2971 requests in 30.04s / 30.03s, 1.21/1.23MB read', 'Socket errors: connect 0, read 0, write 0, timeout 192', recorded latency max 10.26 ms and mean 3.71 ms, and a search of its log for 'Non-2xx' returned no lines.

Observability history here is very short: Loki holds hotel-reservation lines only from 2026-11-21T10:32:35Z onward (a 5-minute count_over_time returns a single point at 10:33:44 with 1169 lines), Prometheus series carry a single sample at 10:34:21, and the sampled Jaeger traces cover roughly 10:33:56-10:34:20, so no comparable pre-incident baseline exists.

hypothesis.text: The object that produces the observed not-ready state is CronJob hotel-reservation/audit-log-archiver: its job template pairs a short-lived archiver container with an endless sidecar ('exec nc -lk -p 24224 -e cat') and defines neither probes, ttlSecondsAfterFinished nor activeDeadlineSeconds, so every per-minute Job stays active forever, each pod keeps a Completed archiver container and never becomes Ready, which explains the pending KubePodNotReady alert without any hotel-reservation application fault.

The intended application-level fault is most plausibly the geo-db or rate-db privilege revocation staged through ConfigMaps failure-admin-geo / failure-admin-rate, which are mounted only into mongodb-geo and mongodb-rate (both rolled to generation 2): if revoke-admin-(geo|rate)-mongo.sh were executed, the 'admin' user used by the geo/rate services would lose readWrite and their MongoDB operations would fail. This remains unconfirmed because no such failure was observed in the sampled window.

The 192 per-round socket timeouts recorded by wrk2 could indicate that a fraction of client connections to the frontend ClusterIP receive no response, but no server-side long spans, non-2xx responses or frontend error log lines were observed in the traced window, so the cause (client-side, service/kube-proxy path, or the load generator itself) is not established.

recommendation.text: If the not-ready archiver pods are undesired, fix them at the CronJob level: bound the sidecar lifetime or give the containers a readiness/liveness probe, or make the one-shot archiver a Job that terminates (drop the eternal 'nc -lk' sidecar), and set ttlSecondsAfterFinished/activeDeadlineSeconds; no change was made during this read-only investigation.

Because the geo-db and rate-db privilege-revocation scripts are already mounted into the running mongodb-geo and mongodb-rate pods, a human should confirm with the experiment owner whether revoke-admin-geo-mongo.sh or revoke-admin-rate-mongo.sh was executed after 10:32:48 (and when), and re-check mongod for authorization-failure entries and geo/rate error logs at that time.

counter_evidence.text: Against an active geo-db/rate-db privilege fault: mongod logs contain no authorization-failure entries, the init scripts granted readWrite to the 'admin' user at 10:32:42 (geo) and 10:32:44 (rate), all app pods are Ready with 0 restarts, all eight service probes succeed, and the sampled frontend spans (including GET /hotels and POST /reservation) are HTTP 200 with single-digit millisecond durations.

Against a resource-exhaustion explanation for the hotel-reservation pods: the container_cpu_cfs_throttled_periods_total rate is 0 for every container in the namespace, and container CPU usage is at most ~0.047 cores (search-567bb6c4b8-qnp7h), ~0.046 (frontend-68745cb99c-cl45r), ~0.030 (rate-65d6967c95-cjvtl).

rejected_hypothesis.text: Rejected as an explanation for app impact: the failing blackbox-ingress-hotel-reservation probe (probe_success=0, probe_http_status_code=0) targets the ingress-nginx controller's URL, not any hotel-reservation service endpoint, while all eight direct service probes in the same namespace return probe_success=1; the probe failure therefore does not evidence a fault in the hotel-reservation application services I measured.

#!/bin/bash


ROOT_USER="root"
ROOT_PWD="root"

ADMIN_USER="admin"
ADMIN_PWD="admin"
READ_WRITE_ROLE="readWrite"
TARGET_DB="geo-db"

echo "Recreating admin user..."

# Connect to MongoDB and create the admin user
mongo admin -u $ROOT_USER -p $ROOT_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.createUser({user: '$ADMIN_USER', pwd: '$ADMIN_PWD', roles:[{role:'userAdminAnyDatabase',db:'admin'}]});"

echo "Admin user recreated"

# Grant readWrite role on the target database
echo "Granting readWrite role to $ADMIN_USER on $TARGET_DB database..."
mongo admin -u $ROOT_USER -p $ROOT_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.grantRolesToUser('$ADMIN_USER', [{role: '$READ_WRITE_ROLE', db: '$TARGET_DB'}]);"

echo "Privileges restored successfully"

ROOT_USER="root"
ROOT_PWD="root"

TARGET_DB="geo-db"
READ_WRITE_ROLE="readWrite"

echo "Waiting for MongoDB to start..."
until mongo --eval "print('waited for connection')" > /dev/null 2>&1; do
  sleep 1
done
echo "MongoDB started"

# Create the admin user (will fail if the user already exists)
echo "Creating admin user..."
mongo admin --eval "db.createUser({user: '$ADMIN_USER', pwd: '$ADMIN_PWD', roles:[{role:'userAdminAnyDatabase',db:'admin'}]});"

# Grant readWrite role on the target database
echo "Granting readWrite role to $ADMIN_USER on $TARGET_DB database..."
mongo admin -u $ADMIN_USER -p $ADMIN_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.grantRolesToUser('$ADMIN_USER', [{role: '$READ_WRITE_ROLE', db: '$TARGET_DB'}]);"

# Create the root user (will fail if the user already exists)
echo "Creating root user..."
mongo admin --eval "db.createUser({user: '$ROOT_USER', pwd: '$ROOT_PWD', roles:[{role:'userAdminAnyDatabase',db:'admin'}]});"

# Grant readWrite role on the target database to root
echo "Granting readWrite role to $ROOT_USER on $TARGET_DB database..."
mongo admin -u $ROOT_USER -p $ROOT_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.grantRolesToUser('$ROOT_USER', [{role: '$READ_WRITE_ROLE', db: '$TARGET_DB'}]);"


echo "Initialization script completed"

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind.
